injury.comment: Vaki (ankle) was a limited participant in Thursday's practice.
injury.longComment: A limited participant for Wednesday's walkthrough, Vaki continued to operate with some restrictions while the Lions held a more traditional practice Thursday. Vaki's involvement in any capacity is nonetheless a good sign for his Week 11 status, though he may need to upgrade to full participation Friday to avoid carrying an injury designation into Sunday's game versus the Buccaneers.

tg.callText: [strong] The Lions' official practice report on Wed Nov 18, 2026 lists him as limited in an estimated walkthrough, and he has played the last two games with this ankle injury, including Week 10 after missing practice Wednesday and Thursday.

injury.comment: Johnston brought in his sole target for six yards in the Chargers' 23-20 win over the Ravens on Monday night.
injury.longComment: The speedster was poised to see some added involvement with Ladd McConkey (back) sidelined, but that never materialized on a night when 86 of Justin Herbert's 129 passing yards went to Tre' Harris. Johnston's yardage total was a season-low figure, and he's now been limited to one reception in four of the last five games. Johnston's often been able to offset the modest catch totals with big plays, but that clearly wasn't the case Monday night. Johnston will remain a hit-or-miss fantasy option in a Week 11 home matchup against the Jets on Sunday, irrespective of McConkey's availability.

injury.comment: Meyers (ankle) was a limited participant in Thursday's practice, Ryan O'Halloran of The Florida Times-Union reports.
injury.longComment: Meyers had his reps capped for a second straight practice, but if he can maintain limited activity or upgrade to full participation Friday, he should be on track to play Sunday against the Giants. The veteran slot receiver has yet to miss a game this season, recording 29 receptions for 408 yards and two touchdowns on 43 targets through nine appearances.

tg.callText: [strong] RotoWire and CBS Sports (Nov 18): limited Wednesday with the ankle injury. The Jaguars often limit him early in the week. He hasn't missed a game this year, including last week after missing Wednesday's practice. Based only on Wednesday's report.

injury.comment: Klubnik completed 11 of 20 passes for 137 yards, no touchdowns and one interception in Sunday's 31-12 loss to the Bills. He added three rushing attempts for 26 yards.
injury.longComment: Klubnik saw the first regular-season action of his NFL career in the second half of Sunday's loss, as Geno Smith (ankle) exited the game. The rookie fourth-round pick led the offense down to Buffalo's four-yard line on his first possession in the third quarter, but the Jets settled for a field goal on that possession, and Klubnik was picked off on his next drive. If Smith isn't ready to return in Week 11, Klubnik would be in line to make his first regular-season start on the road against the Chargers.

injury.comment: Davis (hamstring) remained limited in Thursday's practice.
injury.longComment: It's a new injury for the running back, which clouds his status for Week 11 against the Dolphins. If Davis is unable to handle his normal handful of snaps, Frank Gore could be elevated from the practice squad.

tg.callText: [lean] He was limited on Wednesday, Nov 18 with a hamstring injury, his first time on the injury report since a Week 8 illness, and CBS (Nov 18) said that unless he left practice early Davis should still have decent odds of being ready to play Sunday against the Dolphins.

injury.comment: Johnson recorded two tackles on special teams during the Bears' 27-24 win over the Buccaneers on Sunday.
injury.longComment: Kyle Monangai (thumb/toe) was inactive for a fifth consecutive game, with Johnson operating as the Bears' RB2 behind D'Andre Swift in the Bears' four contests prior to Sunday against the Bucs. However, Johnson didn't play a single offensive snap against Tampa Bay; instead, it was Salvon Ahmed (five carries for 25 yards) who mixed into the backfield as Chicago's complementary piece to Swift. The Bears are on a bye for Week 10, with their next game taking place in Week 11 against the Lions on Sunday, Nov. 22. Johnson would have a narrow path to offensive relevancy if Monangai is cleared to return for that contest.

injury.comment: Knight turned five carries into 19 yards, failed to haul in either of his two targets and recorded a tackle during the Cardinals' 34-6 loss to the Rams on Sunday.
injury.longComment: Knight was cleared to return for Week 10 from a one-game absence while in the league's concussion protocol. His 19 snaps were actually ahead of fellow running back Tyler Allgeier (16), with the duo each logging five carries. The Cardinals logged only 35 offensive snaps for the entire game and finished with a measly 17:37 time of possession, however. It was Arizona's first game with rookie third-rounder Carson Beck under center, and Knight and the offense will have its hands full in Week 11 against Kansas City, whose defense ranks eighth in the NFL in yards allowed per game (314.8).

injury.comment: Douglas (shoulder) is expected to play Sunday against the Bills, Barry Jackson of the Miami Herald reports.
injury.longComment: Douglas said earlier this week that he was planning to play Sunday, and head coach Jeff Hafley backed up that statement while speaking prior to Friday's practice. The Dolphins will reveal whether or not Douglas carries an injury designation into Sunday's contest at some point Friday afternoon.

tg.callText: [strong] He was limited in Wednesday's (Nov. 18) practice with a shoulder injury and wore a red non-contact jersey, but the rookie wideout said afterward that he fully expects to play Sunday against the Bills, per the Miami Herald via RotoWire (Nov. 18).

injury.comment: Pittman (foot) participated in practice Thursday, Nick Farabaugh of PennLive.com reports.
injury.longComment: After being designated for return from injured reserve Wednesday, Pittman was able to return to a limited practice. The WR's presence at Thursday's session implies that there were no setbacks, with the Steelers' upcoming injury report set to reveal his official participation level. In any case, Pittman will need to be activated off IR no later than Saturday afternoon in order to have a chance to play Sunday against the Eagles.

injury.comment: LaPorta caught one of four targets for 16 yards in Sunday's 35-10 win over the Patriots in Munch.
injury.longComment: The Lions didn't need to throw it much, as Drake Maye (ankle) got knocked out of the game for the Patriots early, and LaPorta simply didn't get many chances to make an impact. It was the worst performance of the season for the fourth-year tight end, but LaPorta's gone four straight games without reaching 40 receiving yards or getting into the end zone. He'll try to break out in Week 11 against the Buccaneers.

injury.comment: Winston carried twice for one yard in Thursday's 24-21 loss to the Commanders.
injury.longComment: J.J. McCarthy made his third consecutive start for the Giants, but Winston continued to get sprinkled into the game plan during short-yardage situations. He extended a second-quarter drive that culminated in a Cam Skattebo touchdown by gaining a yard on a fourth-and-one play, but Winston was dropped for no gain on a third-and-one run in the fourth quarter that resulted in a Giants punt. The Giants may continue to turn to Winston for quarterback sneaks in future weeks in an effort to limit the wear and tear on McCarthy.

injury.comment: Daniels is slated to take all of the first-teams reps Wednesday with Baker Mayfield (foot) sidelined for the Buccaneers' first Week 11 practice, Greg Auman of Fox Sports reports.
injury.longComment: While the Buccaneers aren't ruling Mayfield out from playing Sunday in Detroit, the fact that he'll be a spectator in practice coming out of a Week 10 bye suggests that Daniels has the early edge on the Week 11 start. Per Auman, Mayfield appeared to be walking normally off to the side during Wednesday's practice, which could indicate that he'll attempt to test out his strained foot during Thursday's session. The Buccaneers should have some clarity by Friday whether Daniels or Mayfield will draw the start Sunday, with Mayfield's activity (or lack thereof) over the next two days likely to be the determining factor.

injury.comment: Hamstring
Estime carried the ball seven times for six yards and caught his only target for five yards in Sunday's 20-17 loss to Carolina.
injury.longComment: Travis Etienne returned from IR and led the Saints' backfield with 11 touches, although he managed just 34 scrimmage yards, while Alvin Kamara handled five touches and scored two short TDs. Perhaps worse for Estime's role and future value, he was ineffective in short-yardage situations, getting stuffed on three attempts to pick up a first down from two yards out or less, and a miscommunication with Tyler Shough on a handoff led to a lost fumble in the second quarter, although the giveaway was charged to the QB. Estime will try to maintain some share of the workload in a Week 11 meeting with the Bears.

injury.comment: Coleman caught one of three targets for 11 yards during Sunday's 31-12 win over the Jets.
injury.longComment: Coleman failed to reel in multiple passes for the third time in the team's last five contests, and he played just 52 percent of the team's offensive snaps in the contest, his lowest percentage since Week 1. The wide receiver was briefly sidelined while being evaluated for a head injury before returning to the contest, which likely contributed to his lower workload. Coleman will continue to be an unpredictable fantasy option in Week 11 versus the Dolphins.

injury.comment: Wicks (ankle) practiced in a limited capacity Thursday.
injury.longComment: Wicks is seeking his first game action since Week 6 due to an ankle injury, and he still has some work to do after kicking off Week 11 prep with back-to-back capped sessions. Friday's practice report will reveal his odds to play Sunday versus the Steelers.

tg.callText: [lean] Wicks was limited in practice on Wed Nov 18, his first practice since Week 6 after missing Weeks 7–9 with an ankle injury, and CBS says he is "trending toward a return," with PhillyVoice calling him likely to play. It's a lean because this is only his first practice after a long absence and there's

injury.comment: Mayer caught two of three targets for 16 yards in Sunday's 21-13 loss to the Seahawks.
injury.longComment: Jack Bech (seven targets) was the only Las Vegas player to see more than four targets in Fernando Mendoza's first career start. The rookie quarterback targeted 10 different players on his 29 attempts. With Kirk Cousins' efficiency off to Minnesota, Mayer is a low-floor TE2 for fantasy, but he could get a bit of a boost if Brock Bowers' ankle injury causes him to miss time.

injury.comment: McKee will remain in a backup role for Sunday's game against the Steelers after head coach Nick Sirianni announced Wednesday that Joe Milton will serve as the Eagles' starting quarterback for a second straight game, Jeff McLane of The Philadelphia Inquirer reports.
injury.longComment: Though the Eagles dropped a seventh straight game while Milton turned the ball over once and took seven sacks in a Week 9 loss to the Giants, Sirianni saw enough from the third-year signal-caller to hand him at least one more start. While it's conceivable that the Eagles could go back to McKee -- who started Weeks 6 through 8 -- at some point if Milton's performance isn't up to par, rookie fifth-round pick Cole Payton is also on the roster and may get a look before the season winds down.

injury.comment: Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur said Wednesday that he has no new updates on the status of Conner (foot), who is still "working to return to perform," Tyler Drake of ArizonaSports.com reports. "It was not a good injury," LaFleur said.
injury.longComment: Conner hasn't played in a game since Week 3 of last season, when he sustained a right foot/ankle injury that required surgery. Though he was able to participate in individual drills in training camp, he never advanced to team work before being placed on injured reserve with a designation to return Aug. 30. The Cardinals still haven't cleared Conner to practice nearly three months later, which suggests that he either experienced a setback over the summer or plateaued in his recovery. Whatever the case, Conner doesn't seem close to a return, and the chances of him playing at any point this season will grow dimmer with each week that he doesn't practice.

injury.comment: Mitchell turned three carries into four yards, failed to haul in his lone target and returned two kickoffs for 30 yards during the Chargers' 23-20 win over the Ravens on Monday.
injury.longComment: One of Mitchell's carries went for 11 yards, but his other two rushes went for minus-five and minus-two yards, and all of those touches came on the same drive in the second quarter. His 13 offensive snaps were third-most among Chargers running backs behind Kimani Vidal (15) and Omarion Hampton (36), and it was Hampton that commanded the majority of backfield touches, finishing with 22 carries for 105 yards and a touchdown. Mitchell has logged four carries or fewer in three of his last four outings, and he'll continue to operate in a rotational role on offense heading into the Chargers' Week 11 home tilt against the Jets on Sunday.

injury.comment: Bryant caught four of five targets for 56 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 26-21 win over Carolina.
injury.longComment: Bryant was activated from IR on Saturday after recovering from an ankle injury, and he came up big late in Sunday's contest, hauling in a 26-yard TD strike from Bo Nix with less than six minutes left in the fourth quarter for what proved to be the game-winning score. The second-year wideout's clutch play came after Jaylen Waddle (concussion) had left the game, and if a Week 10 bye doesn't give him enough time to recover, Bryant could see an elevated role in Week 11 against the Raiders.

injury.comment: Godwin caught two of three targets for 16 yards and added a 12-yard rush during Sunday night's 27-24 loss to the Bears.
injury.longComment: Godwin has now gone back-to-back weeks without reeling in at least three passes after having done so in each of Tampa Bay's first seven contests this year. The wide receiver has yet to exceed 50 receiving yards or reach the end zone over nine games so far during the 2026 campaign, and he will remain an unappealing fantasy option when the Buccaneers return to action in Week 11 against the Lions.

injury.comment: Shipley (foot) remained limited in practice Thursday.
injury.longComment: Shipley is still on injured reserve but had his 21-day practice window opened this week. With Saquon Barkley healthy right now, Shipley has minimal fantasy appeal in a broken Philadelphia offense that is near the bottom of the league in most categories over the last month.

injury.comment: Wright turned three carries into minus-2 yards, caught both of his targets for 17 yards and returned four kickoffs for 88 yards during the Dolphins' 24-22 loss to the Colts on Sunday.
injury.longComment: Wright's first touch on offense came midway through the second quarter and resulted in a carry for minus-3 yards, although he did connect with Kyle McCord for a 16-yard catch late in the third. Wright was on the field for 12 of the Dolphins' 69 offensive snaps (17.4 percent), which was far behind lead back Ollie Gordon (49 snaps). Wright is averaging only 1.6 YPC on 25 rushes through seven regular-season games, and most of his on-field impact has come on special teams as a returner on kickoffs. The Dolphins will stay on the road for Week 11 against the Bills on Nov. 22.

injury.comment: Worthy failed to catch any of his three targets in Sunday's 35-13 win over the Falcons.
injury.longComment: Worthy ran a team-high 37 routes on Patrick Mahomes' 38 dropbacks, but on a day Mahomes targeted nine different players, Worthy was the only one to not record a catch. With Josh Downs now in the fold and working to get comfortable in the offense, Worthy's role will likely only continue to shrink. On just eight routes in his team debut Sunday, Downs posted a 4-53-1 receiving line on five targets. Worthy hasn't produced that many fantasy points in a game all season. He's waiver-wire fodder in 12-team redraft leagues.

injury.comment: Cooper caught just two of eight targets for 25 yards in Sunday's 19-11 loss to the Giants.
injury.longComment: With DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) still out, Cooper played more than 90 percent of the offensive snaps for the third straight game. He's done very little with that playing time, producing five catches for 61 yards during that span. Cooper is well off the fantasy radar until he shows something in the box score, and that's if Smith and Wicks remain sidelined.

injury.comment: Strange caught two of three targets for nine yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 40-23 win over the Titans.
injury.longComment: The Jaguars keep blowing out their opponents, and Strange contributed a three-yard touchdown Sunday but was otherwise not heard from much, as Parker Washington dog-walked the Titans' secondary for 7-152-1 receiving on nine targets. Strange's touchdown grab was his first since Week 1. He remans a locked-in TE1 for fantasy, as he is playing virtually every snap in an elite offense.

injury.comment: Keenum (coach's decision) is inactive but serving as the Bears' emergency No. 3 quarterback for Sunday Night Football versus the Buccaneers.
injury.longComment: Keenum will once again operate as the team's emergency QB option in Week 9, making it four games in a row in that role. The 38-year-old will only be eligible to enter the game if both starter Caleb Williams and backup Tyson Bagent are forced out of the contest.

injury.comment: Cook was signed to the Dolphins' active roster Tuesday.
injury.longComment: Cook served as the team's No. 2 option at quarterback behind Kyle McCord in the team's 24-22 loss to the Colts in Week 10, with Malik Willis (abdomen) being placed on injured reserve prior to the contest. Cook reverted to the practice squad Monday, but he has now officially become a member of the team's active roster ahead of Sunday's matchup with the Bills.

injury.comment: Head coach Jeff Hafley said Monday that Willis (groin/core) has not undergone surgery and that the Dolphins are still determining if a procedure is needed, David Furones of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports.
injury.longComment: Per Barry Jackson of the Miami Herald, Hafley noted on that subject Monday, "We will see how he feels. If he needs surgery, he will have surgery," while adding that if the QB does undergo a procedure, it wouldn't "necessarily" be season ending. In any case, the earliest Willis can come off IR is Week 14, with Kyle McCord and Brady Cook currently available to handle Miami's signal-caller duties.

injury.comment: Knee - Meniscus
Calf
Minshew (elbow) underwent UCL reconstructive surgery Monday, Jeremy Fowler of ESPN.com reports.
injury.longComment: Though the procedure will bring an end to Minshew's season, he's expected to make a full recovery ahead of the 2027 campaign. The veteran quarterback sustained the injury while making his lone start of the season Week 9 in Seattle, but he played though the elbow issue and completed 21 of 30 passes for 166 yards. Rookie third-round pick Carson Beck took over as the Cardinals' starting quarterback in Week 10 and is expected to lead the offense for the remainder of the season.

injury.comment: Rudolph completed one of three pass attempts for two yards and rushed once for nine yards in Sunday's 38-18 loss to the Bengals.
injury.longComment: After the Bengals had built a 20-point lead with five minutes remaining in the fourth quarter, head coach Mike McCarthy opted to remove starting quarterback Aaron Rodgers from the game and turned to Rudolph to direct the offense for the Steelers' final possession. Rudolph led the Steelers on an 11-play drive that concluded in the red zone before time expired. The 31-year-old Rudolph has now made four relief appearances behind Rodgers on the season, playing limited snaps in each of those contests.

injury.comment: Howard (coach's decision) is inactive and serving as Pittsburgh's emergency third quarterback Sunday night versus Cincinnati.
injury.longComment: Howard has regularly worked in the emergency third-quarterback role this season, though it has yet to result in any game action. He'll be eligible to enter the matchup Sunday night only if both Aaron Rodgers and Mason Rudolph exit due to injury, illness or ejection.

injury.comment: Groin
The Buccaneers signed Stick off their practice squad Monday, Scott Smith of the team's official site reports.
injury.longComment: Stick has been a member of the Buccaneers' practice squad all season, with Tampa Bay having previously elevated him from Weeks 4 through 6 to back up Jalon Daniels while he filled in as the starter in place of Baker Mayfield, who was out due to a dislocated thumb. Mayfield has since moved past that injury, but he's currently nursing a sprained foot coming out of the Buccaneers' Week 9 loss to the Bears. Tampa Bay's decision to sign Stick implies some concern about Mayfield's status heading into Sunday's game against the Lions, potentially setting the stage for Stick to back up Daniels for the fourth time this season.

injury.comment: Slovis (coach's decision) is inactive but serving as the Ravens' emergency No. 3 quarterback Monday night versus the Chargers.
injury.longComment: Slovis will operate as Baltimore's third option at QB for the second straight week. He will only be eligible to enter the game if both starter Jacoby Brissett and backup Joe Fagnano are removed from the contest.

injury.comment: The Ravens believe "there's a chance" that Jackson (thumb) could return for their Week 16 matchup with the Browns, assuming all goes well in his recovery from right thumb surgery, Dan Graziano of ESPN.com reports.
injury.longComment: Last Friday, head coach Jesse Minter announced that Jackson was facing a projected recovery timeline of 6-to-10 weeks after requiring a procedure to address a broken and dislocated thumb. A Week 16 return would be right up against the short end of that timeline, so if Jackson has shown notable improvement by that point, he could push to play if the 4-6 Ravens haven't faded from the playoff picture. While Jackson remains sidelined for at least a few more weeks, the Ravens will entrust trade-deadline acquisition Jacoby Brissett to direct the offense.

injury.comment: Toe
Undisclosed
The Bears placed Scott (wrist) on injured reserve Thursday.
injury.longComment: Scott will be required to miss at least the next four games. He's appeared in four contests this season, playing 65 snaps on special teams.

injury.comment: Undisclosed
Abanikanda reverted to the Cowboys' practice squad Monday, per the NFL's transaction log.
injury.longComment: Abanikanda made his 2026 regular-season debut against the 49ers in Week 10, when he operated as the Cowboys' RB2 behind Javonte Williams. Abanikanda finished that contest with two carries for eight yards and a two-yard catch on his lone target in what ended as a 46-40 loss for Dallas. With both Tyler Goodson (knee) and Malik Davis (hip) on injured reserve, Abanikanda figures to be elevated to the Cowboys' active roster for Week 11 against the Titans on Sunday.

Prentice (concussion) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice.
injury.longComment: It appears Prentice entered the league's concussion protocol following the Broncos' Week 9 win over the Panthers. He had additional time to recover courtesy of the Week 10 bye, so the veteran fullback should be available for Sunday's AFC West tilt against the Raiders.

injury.comment: Saylors rushed twice for nine yards while adding 26 yards as a kick returner during Sunday's 35-10 win over the Patriots.
injury.longComment: Saylors played six snaps on offense while serving as a No. 3 option behind Jahmyr Gibbs and Sione Vaki in the backfield. Saylors was on the field for 20 snaps with the special-teams unit, and he'll continue to be primarily a special-teams asset in Week 11 against the Buccaneers.

injury.comment: Back
Chestnut played all 25 of his snaps on special teams in Sunday's 40-23 win over the Jaguars.
injury.longComment: The fifth-year running back has suited up for all nine of the Titans' games this season, but he's been deployed almost exclusively on special teams as a member of the team's kick coverage and return units. He's played just two offensive snaps on the campaign and hasn't logged any carries or targets.

injury.comment: Ott (hamstring) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice.
injury.longComment: Ott was unable to play against the Falcons in Week 10 due to a hamstring injury. However, the undrafted rookie out of Oklahoma was cleared to practice in full Wednesday, so he should be available for Sunday's home game against the Cardinals. If Kenneth Walker (groin) cannot play in Week 11, then Ott would have the opportunity to serve as the Chiefs' RB2 behind rookie fifth-rounder Emmett Johnson.

injury.comment: Laube played all 22 of his snaps on special teams in Sunday's 21-13 loss to the Seahawks and returned two kickoffs for 46 yards and one punt for zero yards.
injury.longComment: Since earning seven touches in a Week 5 blowout loss to the Patriots, Laube has been an afterthought on offense. He's played just eight total offense snaps in the Raiders' ensuing five games, and Sunday marked the first time all season that he was limited exclusively to special teams.

injury.comment: Allen turned his lone carry into zero yards and hauled in his lone target for minus-4 yards during the Dolphins' 24-22 loss to the Colts on Sunday.
injury.longComment: Allen found the ball on both of his offensive snaps during Sunday's loss, although he ended up losing four yards on his only catch of the game early in the second quarter. He's well behind Ollie Gordon and Jaylen Wright on the running back depth chart, and most of Allen's playing time in Week 11 against the Bills on Nov. 22, likely will come on special teams.

injury.comment: Knee - ACL
Donaldson (shoulder) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice.
injury.longComment: Donaldson missed the Saints' last three games due to a shoulder injury, but his full practice Wednesday indicates that he'll be available for Sunday's road game against the Bears. Even if Donaldson does suit up, his role in the backfield figures to be minimal, seeing as Travis Etienne is off injured reserve and Alvin Kamara and Audric Estime are also available for the Saints.

injury.comment: Knee
Tracy (hamstring) could be reinstated from injured reserve when first eligible ahead of the Giants' Week 13 game against the 49ers, Dan Duggan of The Athletic reports.
injury.longComment: The Giants haven't provided any updates on Tracy since he landed on IR on Oct. 27 after sustaining a hamstring strain in a Week 7 win over the Texans, but the running back is seemingly progressing well and could be ready to play once he sits out the required four games. Once he's reinstated, Tracy could operate as a change-of-pace option behind Cam Skattebo, who appears to have reclaimed the lead role out of the New York backfield after a one-game benching in Week 6.

injury.comment: Davis didn't touch the ball on offense in Sunday's 31-12 loss to the Bills.
injury.longComment: With Breece Hall and Braelon Allen both healthy, Davis has minimal fantasy value, except for leagues that count return yardage. He's played zero offensive snaps over the last two contests, but Davis did return three kickoffs for 74 yards against Buffalo.

injury.comment: Mitchell reverted to the Eagles' practice squad Monday.
injury.longComment: Mitchell has been elevated each of the past three weeks and has logged at least six touches in every game during that span. During this past Sunday's 19-11 loss to the Giants, he recorded six yards on three carries and caught three passes for 20 yards on four targets. The Eagles would need to sign Mitchell to the 53-man roster in order for him to be eligible to play in their next game, which will be Nov. 22 versus Pittsburgh following a Week 10 bye. That opportunity for Mitchell could depend on whether Tank Bigsby (abdomen) and/or Will Shipley (foot) return from injured reserve.

injury.comment: Ankle
Knee
Tucker didn't log any offensive snaps in a loss to the Bears on Sunday. He returned four kickoffs for 92 yards.
injury.longComment: It was the second straight week in which Tucker went without an offensive snap. That's happened despite Tampa Bay going to the ground plenty during that span. Perhaps not coincidentally, Tucker has begun working as a kick returner during the two-game stretch. It appears he's not going to get many opportunities on offense as long as Bucky Irving and Kenny Gainwell are healthy.

injury.comment: Etienne took three carries for one yard and caught both of his two targets for nine yards during Sunday's 20-17 win at New Orleans. He also returned three punts for 43 yards.
injury.longComment: Etienne again played second fiddle to starter Chuba Hubbard in Week 10 with Jonathon Brooks sidelined by a groin injury, and Etienne got his second-most touches of the season. His role on offense in Week 11 will depend on Brooks' status, but the vast majority of the Panthers' snaps at tailback will continue to go to Hubbard.

injury.comment: Allen (hamstring) was a limited participant in Thursday's practice, Ryan O'Halloran of The Florida Times-Union reports.
injury.longComment: Allen is one of three Jaguars running backs on the Week 11 injury report, with Bhayshul Tuten (ankle/foot) and Chris Rodriguez (hand) also tending to health concerns. After being listed as a non-participant Thursday, Tuten appears to be more at risk of sitting out Sunday against the Giants than either Allen or Rodriguez, both of whom have been limited in the Jaguars' first two Week 11 practices.

tg.callText: Questionable

injury.comment: Ali played all 19 of his snaps on special teams in Monday's 23-20 loss to the Chargers.
injury.longComment: For the second week in a row, Ali was deployed exclusively on special teams while the Ravens leaned on Derrick Henry and Justice Hill to handle all the snaps out of the backfield. Ali has logged just seven total snaps on offense all season, carrying six times for 24 yards.

injury.comment: The Ravens reinstated Randall (neck/hamstring) from injured reserve Wednesday, Ryan Mink of the team's official site reports.
injury.longComment: With the rookie fifth-round pick's 21-day evaluation window coming to a close Wednesday, Baltimore added him to the 53-man roster to ensure that he'll be available to play over the rest of the season. The 6-foot-3, 240-pound Randall has been a full participant in practices since Week 8 and should be healthy enough to play Sunday at Carolina, but it's unclear if Baltimore will make him active for that contest. Randall will likely slot in third on the depth chart at running back behind Derrick Henry and Justice Hill, and Rasheen Ali is a key contributor on special teams who could be prioritized ahead of Randall on game days.

injury.comment: Ridley played four offensive snaps and didn't show up on the box score otherwise during the Titans' 40-23 loss to the Jaguars on Sunday.
injury.longComment: Even though Carnell Tate (shoulder) was sidelined for a second consecutive week, Ridley was barely involved in the Titans' offensive game plan. Ridley's four offensive snaps were by far a season low, and his role figures to shrink even more given that Tate is expected to return for Week 11 against the Cowboys on Nov. 22. Wan'Dale Robinson (ankle) could be sidelined for that contest, although those offensive snaps likely will go to Elic Ayomanor, Chimere Dike and even practice-squad wideout Xavier Restrepo rather than Ridley.

injury.comment: Harris secured all five targets for 86 yards in the Chargers' 23-20 win over the Ravens on Monday night.
injury.longComment: With Ladd McConkey (back) sidelined, Harris functioned as a de facto top target for Justin Herbert, and he was responsible for all but 43 of his quarterback's passing yards. The yardage tally also was a career-high figure for Harris, who generated team-high totals with all three components of his receiving line. Harris is up to a career-high 348 receiving yards on 26 catches heading into a favorable Week 11 home matchup against the Jets on Sunday.

injury.comment: Franklin brought in three of four targets for 31 yards during the Broncos' 26-21 win over the Panthers on Sunday.
injury.longComment: Franklin drew a 27-yard pass interference penalty on the Broncos' second offensive play of the game, but the third-year wide receiver didn't log his first catch until early in the fourth quarter. He has operated in a rotational role for most of the season, and even with Jaylen Waddle in the league's concussion protocol, Franklin will likely maintain that workload following the Broncos' Week 10 bye.

injury.comment: Wilson (finger) was a full participant in Thursday's practice.
injury.longComment: With a second full practice under his belt since being designated for return from injured reserve Wednesday, Wilson looks poised to get activated ahead of Sunday's game against the Eagles. Prior to missing time with a dislocated finger and a fractured digit on his left hand, Wilson had averaged five targets per game over his five appearances, but he could struggle to see that level of volume upon returning. Fellow wideout Michael Pittman (foot) was also a full participant in Thursday's practice and could be a candidate to return from IR this week, and rookie second-round pick Germie Bernard may have performed well enough over the last handful of games to retain a notable role in the Steelers' receiving corps.

injury.comment: Freiermuth recorded two catches (on three targets) for 35 yards and one touchdown during Sunday's 38-18 loss in Cincinnati.
injury.longComment: Freiermuth was added to the Steelers' injury report Saturday due to an illness that left him questionable for Week 10 action. Ultimately, he avoided inactive status and also made an end-zone visit for the first time since Week 5 on a 27-yard hookup with QB Aaron Rodgers in the fourth quarter. Considering Freiermuth hasn't reached 50 receiving yards in any game this season, he remains a TD-dependent fantasy option (five in his nine appearances).

injury.comment: Raymond caught four passes for 32 yards on seven targets in Sunday night's 27-24 win over the Bucs.
injury.longComment: Raymond tied Rome Odunze for second on the team in targets behind Luther Burden (nine), but Burden was injured late in the fourth quarter. If he needs to miss any time, Raymond projects to see elevated snaps alongside Odunze and Colston Loveland. The good news for Burden is he'll have two weeks to heal up with the Bears headed into their bye in Week 10.

injury.comment: Head coach Todd Bowles suggested Monday that McMillan (knee) isn't likely to immediately return to action following the Buccaneers' Week 10 bye, Rick Stroud of the Tampa Bay Times reports.
injury.longComment: While Bowles indicated that linebacker Yaya Diaby (knee) has decent odds of playing in the Buccaneers' next game Nov. 22 versus the Lions, the coach was less optimistic about McMillan's chances of being ready to play in Week 11. The Buccaneers have yet to open McMillan's 21-day practice window, after he was placed on injured reserve Sept. 30 due to a PCL sprain in his left knee, which was an aggravation of a previous injury. Bowles noted that McMillan underwent a medical procedure on the knee shortly after landing on IR and is still dealing with some discomfort.

injury.comment: Johnson caught two passes for 28 yards on three targets in Sunday's 20-17 loss to the Panthers.
injury.longComment: With Jordyn Tyson playing his second game since debuting last week, the rookie wideout was targeted 13 times on Tyler Shough's 35 pass attempts. It didn't leave much for the rest of New Orleans' pass catchers, as Travis Etienne was actually second on the team with five targets. Over his last five games, Johnson has nine catches for 85 yards and a score. He's become a low-end TE2 for fantasy.

injury.comment: Ayomanor caught five of 10 targets for 79 yards in Sunday's 40-23 loss to the Jaguars.
injury.longComment: While he wasn't particularly efficient with the volume, Ayomanor led the Titans in targets and receiving yards on the afternoon, , and the receptions and yardage were both career highs, with Carnell Tate (shoulder) sidelined and Wan'Dale Robinson (ankle) exiting the contest early. If they both remain on the shelf in Week 11 against the Cowboys, Ayomanor figures to handle an increased role once again. The second-year WR sports an 18-290-1 line on 36 targets through nine games on the year.

injury.comment: Fields brought in three of four targets for 62 yards in the Giants' 24-21 loss to the Commanders on Thursday.
injury.longComment: The rookie finished a distant second in receiving yards to Isaiah Likely for the Giants on the night, but Fields' yardage total was the second highest of his nascent career. Fields has at least three catches in three consecutive games after opening his career with six straight two-reception efforts, and the Notre Dame product will look to continue cultivating his chemistry with J.J. McCarthy in a Week 11 home matchup against the Jaguars on Sunday, Nov. 22.

injury.comment: Cameron caught all three of his targets for 67 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 40-23, Week 10 win over Tennessee. He also returned five kickoffs for 142 yards.
injury.longComment: Cameron gave the Jaguars a 14-point lead early in the fourth quarter when he hauled in a 25-yard touchdown pass from Trevor Lawrence. It was the rookie wideout's third touchdown of the campaign but his first since Week 3. Cameron's 67 receiving yards marked a career high, while his three receptions tied the most he's had as a pro. Cameron's propensity for finding the end zone (his three TDs have come on just 12 total catches) is appealing, but at this point he isn't getting enough volume to be a reliable week-to-week fantasy asset.

injury.comment: Thomas caught three of four targets for 29 yards in Sunday's 40-23 win over the Titans.
injury.longComment: The three catches tied his season high, while the four targets represented his biggest volume since Week 2. The Jaguars' decision not to deal Thomas at the trade deadline remains a curious one, as the third-year wideout simply doesn't have a significant role in Liam Coen's offense and might not step into one even if someone like Parker Washington got injured -- Josh Cameron was more productive Sunday on three targets and caught one of Trevor Lawrence's three TDs. Thomas will take a 13-146-2 line on 26 targets over nine games into a Week 11 tilt against the Giants.

injury.comment: Ferguson didn't practice Wednesday due to knee and ankle injuries and won't be available for Sunday's game against the Titans, Todd Archer of ESPN.com reports.
injury.longComment: Ferguson injured his knee in a Week 9 win over the Colts, while the ankle issue is more of a lingering concern after he initially sustained a low sprain in a Week 8 loss to the Cardinals. Head coach Brian Schottenheimer previously announced Nov. 9 that Ferguson was set to miss multiple weeks, so the tight end's continued absence from practice comes as little surprise. In Ferguson's stead, Brevyn Spann-Ford should be in line for another turn as Dallas' top tight end in Week 11.

tg.callText: Out

injury.comment: Dike caught two passes for 16 yards on three targets in Sunday's 40-23 loss to the Jaguars. He added five rushing yards on one attempt.
injury.longComment: With Carnell Tate (shoulder) out again, Dike played 54 of 57 offensive snaps against Jacksonville, but his three targets were a distant fifth on the team and represented just an 8.1 percent target share. Outside of his 5-71-1 receiving outburst in Week 8 against Cincinnati, Dike has amassed eight catches for 69 scoreless yards. He's not a reliable fantasy option, though a Week 11 date with Dallas' secondary awaits should Tate remain sidelined.

injury.comment: Virgil was on the field for 16 of the Cardinals' 35 offensive snaps (45.7 percent), but the rookie fifth-rounder didn't get a target during Sunday's 34-6 loss to the Rams.
injury.longComment: The Cardinals' offense struggled in its first game this season with rookie third-rounder Carson Beck under center, finishing with just 17:37 in time of possession. That meant less opportunities for Virgil and the rest of the pass catchers, and even star tight end Trey McBride finished with only five catches on as many targets for 37 yards. It's hard to put much trust into Virgil and the rest of the pass catchers, especially with the team heading into a tough Week 11 road tilt against Kansas City.

injury.comment: Andrews brought in all eight targets for 82 yards in the Ravens' 23-20 loss to the Chargers on Monday.
injury.longComment: According to Ryan Mink of the Ravens' official site, Andrews confirmed after Monday's game that he's been playing through a broken left hand since Week 3, but he finally appears to be back to full health. Though he didn't miss any time due to broken hand, he was listed on the injury report from Weeks 4 through 9 before avoiding the report entirely for Week 10. He proceeded to deliver a season-best performance in starting quarterback Jacoby Brissett's team debut, eclipsing his previous-best mark in receiving yardage by 33 yards. Andrews' instant chemistry with Brissett was certainly encouraging after the Ravens' passing attack's moribund state over the prior two contests, and the veteran tight end could continue thriving in a Week 11 road matchup against the Panthers, especially now that he appears to have fully healed up from the hand injury.

injury.comment: Williams (ribs) won't play in Sunday's game against the Chargers.
injury.longComment: With Omar Cooper (ankle/hip) also slated to be unavailable for the contest, Garrett Wilson and Adonai Mitchell will lead the Jets' Week 11 WR corps, with coach Aaron Glenn noting Friday that the team's tight ends, primarily Kenyon Sadiq and Mason Taylor, should have an opportunity to see added opportunities as pass catchers this weekend in the absence of both Cooper and Williams.

injury.comment: Lane brought in three of 11 targets for 61 yards in the Ravens' 23-20 loss to the Chargers on Monday night.
injury.longComment: Lane was far from efficient during his first opportunity to work with new quarterback Jacoby Brissett, but he parlayed his career-high target total into a career-best yardage tally. The fact the rookie third-round pick garnered so much of Brissett's attention was certainly encouraging, and Lane could emerge as a much more consistent No. 3 option in the offense in coming weeks.

injury.comment: Legette didn't produce any output in the boxscore during Carolina's win over the Saints on Sunday.
injury.longComment: Legette made his return to the lineup after having been sidelined since Week 2 due to a knee injury, but he ended up playing just two snaps on offense. He will look to be more involved during next week's matchup versus the Ravens.

injury.comment: Washington caught one pass for five yards on two targets in Sunday night's loss to the Bengals.
injury.longComment: Aaron Rodgers threw for 143 yards in the game, and most of that came in garbage time in the second half with the score already out of hand. Washington has fewer than 30 receiving yards in seven of nine games played this season and is the epitome of a touchdown-or-bust fantasy option at tight end.

injury.comment: Waller (knee) is practicing again Friday, Joseph Person of The Athletic reports.
injury.longComment: The same applies to fellow TE Tommy Tremble (knee), with both players having logged limited practices Thursday after being deemed 'DNPs' a day earlier. The Panthers' upcoming Friday injury report will clarify the duo's game statuses heading into the weekend. Waller is coming off a two-catch, 24-yard effort on four targets in Week 10 versus the Saints, but the week prior he put up an 8/90/1 receiving line on 10 targets versus the Broncos.

injury.comment: Mooney caught two of five targets for eight yards Thursday in a loss to Washington.
injury.longComment: Mooney logged the third-most targets of any New York pass catcher, but he managed just two short receptions. Efficiency has been an issue for the veteran wideout throughout the campaign, as he's hauled in only 14 of 30 targets through nine contests. Mooney has finished with fewer than 10 yards in four of his past six appearances, so he's not a viable fantasy play at the moment.

injury.comment: Johnson caught two passes for 76 yards on five targets in Sunday night's 27-24 loss to the Bears.
injury.longComment: Johnson accounted for the Bucs' longest play of the game, producing a 58-yard catch-and-run to lead the team in receiving yards. Johnson has been working as the Bucs' WR3 behind Emeka Egbuka and Chris Godwin, with rookie Ted Hurst mixing in for sub-package snaps. Johnson isn't a particularly exciting fantasy bet.

injury.comment: Metchie caught his only target for four yards Sunday in a 20-17 win against New Orleans.
injury.longComment: Metchie's only catch and target came late in the third quarter, as he logged four yards on a third-down play to help set up a Ryan Fitzgerald field goal. The veteran wideout had a streak of six games with multiple catches snapped in the Carolina victory. Metchie finished third among Panthers wideouts with 23 offensive snaps, and he's produced like a No. 3 receiver this year, logging no more than three catches and 40 yards in any of his eight games to date.

injury.comment: Hunter caught both of his targets for 16 yards, recorded a three-yard carry and contributed five tackles (three solo) and an interception during the Jaguars' 40-23 win over the Titans on Sunday.
injury.longComment: Fifty-six of Hunter's 62 snaps Sunday came on defense, and that's where he made his biggest impact with a diving interception on a Cam Ward pass intended for Elic Ayomanor, and the Jaguars offense converted that takeaway into a field goal 10 plays later. Hunter's impact on both sides of the ball has been undeniable: he has 28 catches (on 45 targets) for 298 yards and a touchdown, along with 36 tackles (24 solo) and seven pass defenses (including three interceptions) through nine regular-season games. The Jaguars will hit the road for Week 11 against the Giants on Nov. 22.

injury.comment: Otton caught four of eight targets for 25 yards in Sunday night's 27-24 loss to the Bears.
injury.longComment: The tight end saw a team-high eight targets, drawing a 26.7 percent target share from Baker Mayfield. It still didn't translate into much in the box score, as Otton remains without a touchdown through nine games. He's turned 38 targets into 23 catches for 211 yards this season and is a low-floor fantasy option most weeks.

injury.comment: Helm caught all four of his targets for 23 yards in Sunday's 40-23 loss to the Jaguars.
injury.longComment: After a career day last time out in Week 8 against the Bengals, Helm's box score looked more familiar against Jacksonville's stout defense. He's been held below 30 yards in eight of nine games this season and has yet to catch a touchdown. Helm is a member of the large bucket of low-floor TE2 options in fantasy.

injury.comment: Mims caught one of two targets for zero yards, added a five-yard carry and returned three punts for 22 yards during the Broncos' 26-21 win over the Panthers on Sunday.
injury.longComment: Nineteen of Mims' 24 snaps came on offense, although he logged only two touches in the process. He hasn't seen more than four targets in a game this season, with most of his output coming on special teams as a returner on both kickoffs and punts. The Broncos are on a bye for Week 10, so their next game will take place in Week 11 against the Raiders on Sunday, Nov. 22

injury.comment: Allen caught two of four targets for 44 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 35-13 win over the Falcons.
injury.longComment: The rookie wideout scored his first career touchdown by beating the cornerback on a stutter-go for a 39-yard touchdown in the third quarter. With Josh Downs still getting comfortable and learning the offense following Tuesday's acquisition from the Colts, Allen maintained a significant role on offense, playing 22 of 64 offensive snaps. Once Downs progresses from the 10 snaps he played against Atlanta, it will be interesting to see if Allen can push Xavier Worthy (zero catches on three targets across 56 snaps on Sunday) for a larger piece of the outside receiver role in Kansas City's offense.

injury.comment: Fehoko finished Sunday's 34-6 loss to the Rams with one catch on two targets for 21 yards. He also recorded a tackle.
injury.longComment: Week 10 was the Cardinals' first game with rookie third-rounder Carson Beck as the starting quarterback. The offense struggled to move the ball and logged only 35 snaps as a whole while finishing with 17:37 in time of possession. That meant less opportunities for Fehoko and the rest of the Cardinals' skill-position players, although the sixth-year pro did connect with Beck on a 21-yard pass early in the first quarter. Fehoko's 26 offensive snaps led all Arizona wide receivers, and with Michael Wilson (neck) out for the rest of the season, he should continue to operate in an elevated role heading into Week 11 against Kansas City on Nov. 22.

injury.comment: Bateman brought in three of five targets for 42 yards in the Ravens' 23-20 loss to the Chargers on Monday night.
injury.longComment: Bateman put together a solid performance during his first opportunity to work with Jacoby Brissett, posting his best receiving yardage total since Week 5. The veteran wideout also recorded multiple receptions for the first time in three games, and two of his three catches went for first downs. Bateman seemed to lay a solid foundation with his new signal-caller, and he'll look to continue building on it in a Week 11 road matchup against the Panthers.

injury.comment: Gadsden hauled in his lone target for seven yards in Monday's 23-20 win over Baltimore.
injury.longComment: Gadsden went to the locker room during the first half of Monday's game after being poked in the ye, but the second-year tight end was cleared to return for the second quarter. However, his 12 offensive snaps were his lowest since Week 1 against the Cardinals (10), and that lack of playing time coincided with the return of veteran tight end David Njoku, who missed the Chargers' six prior games while on IR due to a fibula injury. Njoku and Charlie Kolar appear to be the Chargers' top options at tight end, squeezing Gadsden out of the game plan ahead of Week 11 against the Jets on Sunday.

injury.comment: TeSlaa caught two of five targets for 19 yards and a touchdown during the Lions' 35-10 win over the Patriots on Sunday in Munich. He also recorded a tackle.
injury.longComment: It was a quiet day for TeSlaa, with the Lions' offense being powered by usual suspects Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jahmyr Gibbs, with the latter duo combining for four touchdowns (three receiving, one rushing). TeSlaa was the other Lions player to find the end zone, which took place early in the second quarter on a 12-yard touchdown pass from Jared Goff. It was the first touchdown catch of the season for TeSlaa, who found the end zone six times across 17 regular-season games during his rookie campaign in 2025. He has been the Lions' distant WR3 behind St. Brown and Jameson Williams, and that shouldn't change ahead of the team's Week 11 tilt against the Buccaneers on Nov. 22.

injury.comment: Armstrong caught his only target for a 43-yard touchdown in Sunday's 35-13 win over the Falcons.
injury.longComment: The wideout played just 17 of 64 offensive snaps against Atlanta and ran only seven pass routes on Patrick Mahomes' 38 dropbacks. Armstrong was tasked with blocking duties on 10 of his snaps. He still managed to catch his first career touchdown in the fourth quarter with the game already well out of hand. Armstrong is not on the fantasy radar.

injury.comment: Nailor recorded one reception for minus-1 yard on four targets in Sunday's 21-13 loss to the Seahawks.
injury.longComment: Making his first NFL start, No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza was under siege throughout the afternoon, as a ferocious Seahawks defense sacked him six times and limited him to just 143 passing yards on 29 attempts. As a result, Nailor and the Raiders' other pass catchers were held quiet, with running back Ashton Jeanty (four receptions for 46 yards) being the only Las Vegas player to top two catches and 25 receiving yards. Though Mendoza will get some more favorable matchups over the Raiders' final seven games, Nailor will be difficult to count on for production. Even while Kirk Cousins served as the starting quarterback for Las Vegas before being traded to the Vikings last week, Nailor was limited to just 14 receptions for 122 yards and one touchdown on 28 targets through eight appearances.

injury.comment: Duvernay caught two of three targets for 35 yards during the Cardinals' 34-6 loss to the Rams on Sunday.
injury.longComment: Duvernay was on the field for only 10 of the Cardinals' 35 offensive snaps (28.6 percent), but the veteran wide receiver connected with rookie third-round quarterback Carson Beck on passes of four and 31 yards on back-to-back plays late in the first quarter. Duvernay finished the contest second in catches, targets and receiving yards behind Trey McBride, and he's caught two passes in each of his last three outings. With Michael Wilson (neck) out for the year, the Cardinals' top wideouts for the rest of the season appear to be Duvernay, Simi Fehoko and rookie fifth-rounder Reggie Virgil, which doesn't inspire much confidence heading into Week 11 against Kansas City on Nov. 22.

injury.comment: Spann-Ford caught one of three targets for 26 yards during the Cowboys' 46-40 loss to the 49ers on Sunday.
injury.longComment: Spann-Ford operated as the Cowboys' No. 1 tight end in Week 10 due to the absence of Jake Ferguson (knee). However, George Pickens, CeeDee Lamb and Ryan Flournoy were the top targets for Dak Prescott. Ferguson is expected to be sidelined for multiple weeks while recovering from his injury, so Spann-Ford should once again top the depth chart in Week 11 against a Titans team that has given up 40-plus points in each of its last two games.

injury.comment: Taylor caught all four of his targets for 20 yards during the Jets' 31-12 loss to the Bills on Sunday.
injury.longComment: Taylor's four catches were tied with Breece Hall and Isaiah Williams for second most on the Jets behind Garrett Wilson, who turned 14 targets into a 7-106-1 line. It was the third time this season that Taylor recorded at least four catches, with his last instance being Week 7 against the Dolphins (five receptions). The second-year tight end has a 22-167-2 line on 29 targets through eight regular-season games heading into Week 11 against the Chargers on Nov. 22.

injury.comment: Bills head coach Joe Brady said Wednesday that Shavers (knee) has been reinstated from the PUP list, Katherine Fitzgerald of The Buffalo News reports.
injury.longComment: Shavers' 21-day evaluation window was set to close this week, so the Bills elected to add him back to the 53-man roster to ensure that he would be available to play this season. The wideout has been a full practice participant for the past two weeks, so he appears to be fully recovered from the torn ACL he sustained in January and should be available for Sunday's game against the Dolphins. If active for the Week 11 contest, Shavers will likely slot in as a depth option at receiver behind the trio of DJ Moore, Khalil Shakir and Keon Coleman.

Thomas hauled in one of his two targets for 13 yards and returned three kicks for 88 yards during Chicago's win versus Tampa Bay on Sunday.
injury.longComment: Thomas continues to see limited action offensively, playing just five snaps Sunday and no more than 15 on offense in any game this season, though he did manage to record his seventh reception of the season. The rookie third-round pick should continue to see the majority of his action come on special teams, and he's now amassed 715 kick-return yards across nine outings this season.

injury.comment: Turpin is expected to resume return duties on both kickoffs and punts Sunday against the Titans, Calvin Watkins of The Dallas Morning News reports.
injury.longComment: The wide receiver had to sit for three games with a rib injury before coming back for last Sunday's loss to the 49ers, in which he fielded punts but not kickoffs. Turpin has 574 kickoff-return yards and 108 punt-return yards on the year.

Restrepo, whom the Titans signed off their practice squad Tuesday, could be in store for more playing time out of the slot moving forward after Tennessee placed Wan'Dale Robinson (ankle) on injured reserve, Mark Mihalko of USA Today reports.
injury.longComment: A 2025 undrafted free agent who played alongside Cam Ward during their final collegiate seasons at Miami, Restrepo showed immediate chemistry with the Titans' second-year quarterback during a 40-23 loss to the Jaguars in Week 10. Restrepo went on to play 19 snaps following Robinson's exit late in the third quarter and notched three receptions for 31 yards on three targets over the game's final 10 minutes. While the Titans are expected to get rookie first-round pick Carnell Tate (shoulder) back for Sunday's game in Dallas, Restrepo's strong showing in relief of the injured Robinson last week should at least allow him to stick ahead of Calvin Ridley (four snaps in Week 10) as Tennessee's No. 4 wideout.

Bech caught two of seven targets for 10 yards during the Raiders' 21-13 loss to the Seahawks on Sunday.
injury.longComment: Bech was the favorite target of rookie first-overall pick Fernando Mendoza, who was making his first career start Sunday after the Raiders shipped Kirk Cousins to the Vikings at the Nov. 10 trade deadline. Bech's seven targets were a season high, but he mustered only two catches for his efforts, and he failed to connect on each of the last four passes he saw from Mendoza in the fourth quarter. The volume appears to be there for Bech, and he could take on a larger role offensively in Week 11 against the Broncos on Nov. 22 if star tight end Brock Bowers (ankle) is unable to play.

injury.comment: Thornton (back) was a full participant in Las Vegas' practice Wednesday, Sam Warren of The Athletic reports.
injury.longComment: Thornton is healthy again after sitting out the team's Week 10 loss to the Seahawks due to a back injury. However, it is still unlikely that the 23-year-old plays in Sunday's matchup versus the Broncos, as Thornton had been a healthy scratch every week since returning from injured reserve in late October prior to Week 10.

injury.comment: Young went without a target while playing one of the Raiders' 59 snaps on offense in Sunday's 21-13 loss to the Seahawks. He also brought back one kickoff for 29 yards.
injury.longComment: Young has suited up in each of the Raiders' 10 games this season, but he's been deployed almost exclusively on special teams. He's seen single-digit snaps on offense in five straight games and has posted a collective 2-36-0 receiving line on three targets on the campaign.

injury.comment: Bell (knee) remained a limited participant in Thursday's practice, David Furones of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports.
injury.longComment: After being sidelined first time this season during this past Sunday's 24-22 loss to the Colts, Bell told Joe Schad of The Palm Beach Post that his absence was a result of hyperextending his knee in a recent practice. The rookie wideout appears to be healthier in Week 11, however, as he was able to practice in a limited fashion for a second straight day. Bell expects be available for Sunday's game against the Bills, per Furones.

tg.callText: [lean] He was inactive for Week 10 against the Colts, but after head coach Jeff Hafley described Bell as day-to-day prior to Wednesday's session, the receiver was able to turn in a limited practice (Nov. 18), so he's slightly more likely than not to play.

injury.comment: Coleman logged one catch for six yards on six targets in Sunday's Week 10 loss to Indianapolis.
injury.longComment: Coleman couldn't get on the same page as QB Kyle McCord, who made his first NFL regular-season appearance. In fact, Coleman has been quiet inefficient regardless of who has thrown him the ball this year, as he has just nine receptions on 27 targets through nine games. Two of his nine catches have been touchdowns, but he's not getting enough touches to be a trustworthy fantasy option.

injury.comment: Wayne (quadriceps) did not participate at practice Wednesday, David Furones of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports.
injury.longComment: Wayne sat out Sunday's game at Indianapolis with a quad injury, and his availability for Week 11 is now in question. If he's not able to get back onto the practice field Thursday or Friday, he'll be trending toward missing Sunday's game at Buffalo.

tg.callText: Questionable

injury.comment: Lance returned three kickoffs for 55 yards during the Saints' 20-17 loss to the Panthers on Sunday.
injury.longComment: The rookie fourth-rounder didn't see a target from Tyler Shough during Sunday's loss, and Lance has not recorded a catch in each of his last two outings, coinciding with the return of 2026 first-round wide receiver Jordyn Tyson. Lance's nine offensive snaps were a season low, and he figures to be limited to return duties now that Tyson is back in the fold. The Saints will hit the road for Week 11 against the Bears on Nov. 22.

injury.longComment: Week 9 was the Eagles' first game with Joe Milton as the starter, with Tanner McKee relegated to backup duties. Milton completed 18 of his 34 passes, and his lone connection with Moore resulted in a three-yard loss. The Eagles are on a bye for Week 10, and Moore's role on the offense would evaporate if one or both of DeVonta Smith (hamstring) or Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) was cleared to play in Week 11 against the Steelers on Sunday, Nov. 22.

Wallace recorded a nine-yard reception on his lone target in Sunday's 34-6 loss to the Rams.
injury.longComment: Though he played just five of the Cardinals' 35 snaps on offense, Wallace was able to come away with his first NFL reception in the third quarter. Even if Wallace earns more playing time in future weeks, he'll likely struggle to produce meaningful fantasy lines while rookie third-round pick Carson Beck continues to direct the offense behind a shaky offensive line.

Thompson (hamstring) is inactive for Monday night's game against the Ravens.
injury.longComment: Thompson will not suit up for Monday's primetime clash after being listed as doubtful following a third consecutive DNP on Saturday, and it's no surprise the fourth-round rookie is unable to play in Monday's game. Derius Davis will take on the role of No. 4 wide receiver in the contest behind starters Quentin Johnston, Tre' Harris and KeAndre Lambert-Smith.

injury.comment: Hurst failed to haul in his lone target during the Buccaneers' 27-24 loss to the Bears on Sunday.
injury.longComment: For a third consecutive game, the rookie third-rounder didn't record a catch while seeing only one target. Of more concern was the fact that Hurst was on the field for only one offensive snap in Week 9 after logging at least 25 offensive snaps in each of the first eight games of the regular season. That lack of offensive playing time coincided with the return of Emeka Egbuka, although Hurst also saw less snaps than Chris Godwin (62), Tez Johnson (52) and even David Sills (six), although Sills was cut by the Buccaneers on Tuesday. With the Buccaneers on a bye for Week 10, Hurst will look for better results in Week 11 against the Lions on Sunday, Nov. 22.

injury.comment: Johnson played all 17 of his snaps on special teams and recorded one tackle in Sunday's 27-24 loss to the Bears.
injury.longComment: Johnson, a reserve wide receiver, has been used almost exclusively on special teams through his two-plus seasons in Tampa Bay. He's logged just 15 total snaps on offense through nine games in 2026, recording a three-yard reception on two targets. Johnson leads the Buccaneers with 14 kickoff returns for 389 yards, but he didn't see any runback opportunities in Week 9 while Sean Tucker handled those duties.

injury.comment: Knee
Engram caught four of five targets for 33 yards in Sunday's 26-21 win over the Panthers.
injury.longComment: The four catches matched Engram's season high, and his 33 yards were his most since Week 5. It goes without saying, but Engram is well off the fantasy radar at tight end. He has 17 catches for 169 yards and one touchdown through nine games, averaging a career-low 18.8 yards per contest.

injury.comment: Njoku played 19 offensive snaps but didn't get a target during Monday's 23-20 win over the Ravens on Monday.
injury.longComment: Njoku's snap count was predictably capped as he returned from a six-game absence due to a fibula injury that he sustained in Week 2 against the Raiders. His 19 offensive snaps were actually ahead of Oronde Gadsden (12), with Charlie Kolar leading all Chargers tight ends with 41 snaps on offense. With another week under his belt to get back up to speed, Njoku could be more involved in the Chargers' passing attack in Week 11 against the Jets on Sunday.

injury.comment: Tremble (knee) was limited in Thursday's practice, Mike Kaye of ESPN.com reports.
injury.longComment: Both Tremble and Darren Waller (knee) were upgraded to limited work after being DNP on Wednesday. Friday's participation levels and injury designations will tell a better story for their Week 11 availability versus Baltimore. Mitchell Evans, Feleipe Franks and Ja'Tavion Sanders are next in line at tight end for Carolina.

injury.comment: Sadiq was limited to a three-yard reception on two targets in Sunday's 31-12 loss to the Bills.
injury.longComment: On a day in which quarterbacks Geno Smith (ankle) and Cade Klubnik dropped back 45 times, Sadiq wasn't able to see much involvement in the passing game. Though the rookie first-round pick put his pass-catching chops on display with a 7-105-1 receiving line in Week 3 against Detroit, he's since delivered a collective 10-95-0 line on 19 targets over the Jets' ensuing seven contests. A lack of extended playing time has been a factor in Sadiq's listless production of late; he's logged fewer than 50 percent of the offensive snaps in five of those seven games while second-year tight end Mason Taylor typically has handled larger snap shares.

injury.comment: Knox caught one of his three targets for seven yards in the Bills' 31-12 win over the Jets on Sunday.
injury.longComment: Knox continues to receive targets as the No. 2 tight end in the Bills offense. The 30-year-old has consistently struggled to bring in catchable balls over the past few contests but remains a valuable part of Buffalo's 13-personnel packages as a blocker and receiving threat. Knox played 41 offensive snaps in Sunday's game and was on the field for 72 percent of the Bills' offensive plays.

injury.comment: Fant failed to haul in his lone target during the Saints' 20-17 loss to the Panthers on Sunday.
injury.longComment: Fant didn't connect with Tyler Shough on a short pass late in the first quarter, and that ended up being the only target for the veteran tight end. Fant has a 12-96-3 line on 19 targets through eight regular-season games, although he's logged one reception or zero in four of his last five outings. He doesn't have much fantasy appeal as the Saints' TE2 behind Juwan Johnson heading into Week 11 against the Bears on Nov. 22.

injury.comment: Gray caught one of three targets for six yards during Sunday's 35-13 win over the Falcons.
injury.longComment: Gray was unable to reel in multiple passes for the second straight week after he had at least two catches in each of the team's previous five games prior to Week 9. The tight end did play a season-high 53 offensive snaps with Travis Kelce being limited to just 18 snaps on offense as a result of an ankle injury. If Kelce is forced to be limited or even miss the team's Week 11 matchup with Arizona, Gray would stand to operate as the team's primary tight end in his place.

injury.comment: Kolar (concussion) remained sidelined for Thursday's practice.
injury.longComment: The tight end remains in concussion protocol and looks like he'll miss Sunday's game against the Jets. If so, Oronde Gadsden and David Njoku would step in to handle most of the tight-end duties.

tg.callText: [toss-up] The Nov. 18 team report lists Kolar as DNP with a concussion. He hasn't cleared the concussion protocol, and after a Monday night game he has a short week to do it. Watch whether he clears the protocol in Thursday and Friday reports.

injury.comment: Higgins played 24 of 35 offensive snaps (68.6 percent) but didn't get a target during the Cardinals' 34-6 loss to the Rams on Sunday.
injury.longComment: Week 10 was Higgins' first game since signing a three-year contract extension worth up to $26.8 million. He didn't have much to show for it during Sunday's loss, although the Cardinals finished with a measly 17:37 time of possession, and the offense struggled as a whole with rookie third-rounder Carson Beck under center. Higgins will take an 18-162-1 receiving line on 20 targets through 10 games into Arizona's Week 11 tilt against Kansas City on Nov. 22.

injury.comment: Bellinger caught two of three targets for six yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 40-23 loss to the Jaguars.
injury.longComment: The blocking specialist played 28 of 57 offensive snaps and was asked to block on 12 of those plays. His two-yard touchdown in the second quarter was Bellinger's first of the season. For the year, Bellinger has 11 grabs for 76 yards and the score on 18 targets across nine contests.

injury.comment: Hawes (shoulder) was a late addition to Wednesday's injury report, Katherine Fitzgerald of The Buffalo News.
injury.longComment: It is unclear whether Hawes suffered his shoulder injury, however, his eligibility for Week 11 against the Dolphins will likely be decided during the Thursday and Friday prep sessions. The 25-year-old will need to upgrade to a full participant by Friday's practice to avoid any injury designation ahead of Sunday's contest.

injury.comment: Roush caught both of his two targets for 23 yards during Sunday's 27-24 win versus the Buccaneers.
injury.longComment: Roush, who has been utilized heavily as a blocker through nine games, achieved a new career high in receiving yards in Week 9. Roush has been relatively efficient with his limited targets so far this season, but Colston Loveland should be expected to continue to handle a substantial majority of the Bears' pass-catching duties at tight end as long as he's available.

injury.longComment: The Cowboys technically still have one elevation to use on Mitchell this season, but they instead will opt to sign him to the active roster for Week 10. His signing gives the Cowboys extra depth at tight end, as the team will be without Jake Ferguson (knee) for Sunday's game against the 49ers.

Trautman caught two of three passes for 15 yards during the Broncos' 26-21 win over the Panthers on Sunday.
injury.longComment: Trautman failed to record a catch across six games between Weeks 2 and 7, but he has logged two receptions in each of his two outings. His 41 offensive snaps ended up being ahead of fellow tight end Evan Engram (38), although the latter has been more involved in the Broncos' offensive game plan than Trautman. The Broncos' next game takes place in Week 11 against the Raiders on Sunday, Nov. 22.

injury.comment: The Broncos opened Lohner's (lower body) 21-day practice window Wednesday, Parker Gabriel of The Denver Post reports.
injury.longComment: Lohner opened the season on injured reserve after undergoing a procedure on his lower body in June. It appears the 25-year-old could make his return soon, as the Broncos have 21 days to officially activate him from IR before he becomes ineligible to return in 2026.

injury.comment: Wright caught both of his targets for 11 yards during the Lions' 35-10 win over the Patriots on Sunday in Munich.
injury.longComment: Wright tied season highs in both receiving yards and catches during Sunday's win, and his 39 snaps on offense were second-most among Lions tight ends behind Sam LaPorta (56). Wright has accumulated seven catches on eight target for 42 yards across nine regular-season games, and he's mostly served as a blocking tight end on the Lions' offense.

injury.comment: Conklin went without a target while playing 22 of the Lions' 71 offensive snaps in Sunday's 35-10 win over the Patriots in Munich.
injury.longComment: A healthy inactive for two of the Lions' first four games of the season, Conklin has now suited up for five consecutive contests. However, the veteran tight end has been handling a limited role, logging less than one-third of the offensive snaps in any of his seven appearances on the season while compiling a 2-11-0 receiving line on three targets.

injury.comment: Pectoral
Briningstool caught one of two targets for 20 yards in Sunday's 35-13 win against the Jets on Sunday.
injury.longComment: Briningstool connected with Patrick Mahomes for a 20-yard reception midway through the first quarter but didn't record another reception. The 23-year-old tight end has exactly one catch in each of his past three games. That's not enough production to warrant fantasy consideration, but Briningstool is at least showing growth as a pass catcher, as he had just one catch on two targets over his first six contests of the campaign.

injury.comment: The Chiefs placed Wiley (ankle) on injured reserve Wednesday, Matt Derrick of ChiefsDigest.com reports.
injury.longComment: Wiley was carted to the locker room in the first quarter of the Chiefs' Week 10 win over the Falcons with an ankle injury. The tight end will now be on IR as he nurses his fractured ankle until at least the latter part of the regular season. Travis Kelce, Noah Gray and Jake Briningstool are now the only tight ends on the Chiefs' active roster.

Johnson logged one catch (on three targets) for eight yards Thursday in a loss to the Commanders.
injury.longComment: Johnson hasn't been able to get going in 2026, as he's finished with one or zero catches in six of his seven games so far. After working as New York's top tight end last season, he's been mostly an afterthought in the current campaign due to the arrival of Isaiah Likely, who went off for a 9-127-1 line on a team-leading 11 targets Thursday. As long as Likely is healthy, Johnson won't have much appeal in most fantasy formats.

injury.comment: Stowers failed to catch his only target in Sunday's 19-11 loss to the Giants.
injury.longComment: The rookie tight end ran just four routes on Joe Milton's 48 dropbacks against the G-Men. Grant Calcaterra ran just six, as the Eagles used more three-wide sets than multiple TE sets. Stowers would need a Dallas Goedert injury or trade to come into any fantasy value.

injury.comment: The Eagles signed Ertz from the practice squad to the active roster Monday.
injury.longComment: Philadelphia is coming off a Week 10 bye, but prior to the midseason respite, there were no reported injuries in the TE group on the active roster. When the position group was depleted earlier this season, the team used elevations on Ertz from Weeks 3-5, but his snap share decreased game by game (38, 21 and 11 percent), while he hauled in three of eight targets for 22 yards in that span. Wednesday's practice report will reveal if any of Dallas Goedert, Eli Stowers, Johnny Mundt or Grant Calcaterra are banged up at the moment.

injury.comment: Ankle
Cuevas caught all three of his targets for 37 yards during Monday night's 23-20 loss to the Chargers.
injury.longComment: Cuevas had an immediate connection with new starting quarterback Jacoby Brissett, reeling in at least three passes for the second time this season and the first time since Week 6. The tight end ranked fourth at his position with 11 offensive snaps, sitting behind Mark Andrews (40), Matthew Hibner (22) and Nick Vannett (14). Cuevas has now caught 13 of 16 targets for 171 yards and a touchdown over 10 contests so far during the 2026 campaign.
